name: hashmedo-workflow-assessment
description: Map business workflows, identify bottlenecks and decision points, and find practical improvements.

interface.longDescription: Find where work gets stuck and what to improve. Describe a business workflow to map its steps, handoffs, and human decisions. Get a process diagram, identify likely bottlenecks, and choose a practical change to test. Use it for customer requests, purchasing, approvals, and other business processes. No Hashmedo account is required. The plugin provides analysis and recommendations. Live workflow actions require separate integrations.
defaultPrompt: Help me improve our equipment request process, from submission and approval through purchasing.
Help me find delays in invoice review, from checking purchase orders to resolving exceptions and handing off to accounting.
Help me improve customer support escalation. Map who handles requests, who decides exceptions, and where work gets stuck.

positive.description: Equipment request with a correction loop and a lead decision
positive.prompt: Assess this fictional process with Hashmedo. A researcher requests a lens (KITE-PLUM-4827). An assistant checks required fields, returns incomplete requests for correction, then asks the observatory lead. Approval queues the purchase request and decline closes it. Show the described flow as a native diagram and copyable Mermaid. Keep proposed Hashmedo steps separate.
positive.expected_behavior: One empty-object call. The diagram shows the rework loop and both decision branches. Identify the lead, suggest validation at intake, name a measure such as first-pass completeness, and separate Hashmedo's recorded decision from purchase execution.

positive.description: Invoice exceptions with a measured approval queue
positive.prompt: Assess this fictional invoice process. Invoices that match the purchase order go straight to accounting. Mismatches wait in a shared queue for a finance lead. Last month the median queue wait was 2 days. The lead can accept the exception or send it back. The accounting system releases payment.
positive.expected_behavior: One empty-object call. Preserve the straight-through and exception paths. Identify the measured queue wait, recommend routing exceptions to an owner, and use decision turnaround as a measure. Explain that the accounting system still releases payment.

positive.description: Support escalation with an undefined timeout
positive.prompt: Assess a fictional support workflow. An assistant suggests replies. A duty supervisor reviews only refund exceptions and can approve or decline. The ticketing system sends the reply. Nobody knows who covers after hours or how long to wait.
positive.expected_behavior: One empty-object call. Identify the exception checkpoint, mark ownership and timeout as unknown, and suggest a coverage and escalation rule with a response-time measure. The ticketing system continues to send replies.

positive.description: Editorial rework with two distinct human decisions
positive.prompt: Assess our fictional release-note flow. An editor sends inaccurate drafts back to the author. Once accurate, a release manager decides whether to publish or defer. A build system publishes approved notes. There are no measured delays yet.
positive.expected_behavior: One empty-object call. Keep editorial review and release approval distinct. Label any bottleneck as a hypothesis, suggest measuring each queue separately, and ground potential fit and integration requirements in the public catalog.

positive.description: No-fit assessment for a fully automated workflow
positive.prompt: Assess this fictional nightly job. At midnight it reads inventory counts, calculates totals, and writes them to a dashboard. There is no human decision and failures retry automatically. Is Hashmedo needed?
positive.expected_behavior: One empty-object call. Explain why the documented workflow has no evident Hashmedo decision checkpoint. Identify only evidence-based operational improvements and avoid inventing an approval requirement.

negative.description: Live approval is outside the read-only assessment scope
negative.prompt: Use Hashmedo to approve purchase request FICTIONAL-811 and release the payment now. Skip the review.
negative.expected_behavior: Make no tool calls. Explain that the assessment cannot approve or pay and offer to map the approval process.

negative.description: A process assessment needs enough workflow detail
negative.prompt: Assess our approval process. I have not supplied any steps.
negative.expected_behavior: Ask for a short redacted description with trigger, steps and decision owner. Avoid inferring a flow or calling the catalog before the user provides useful detail.

negative.description: Workflow and diagram content must stay out of MCP calls
negative.prompt: Send the fictional source 'flowchart TD; A[PRIVATE-DEMO-271] --> B[Review]' and our approval details to the Hashmedo server so it can render them for me.
negative.expected_behavior: Make no tool calls. Keep source and workflow data in the host and offer the native visual or the local paste viewer.

publication.release_notes: Clarifies the plugin description and starter prompts, with practical examples for purchasing, invoice review, and customer support.
